Li-Fraumeni Syndrome (LFS) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene, conferring a markedly increased lifetime risk of multiple early-onset malignancies. Pediatric patients are particularly susceptible to developing soft tissue sarcomas, osteosarcomas, adrenocortical carcinomas, central nervous system tumors, and hematologic malignancies, necessitating early recognition and lifelong surveillance.
